topic: Can we more effectively diagnose and treat complex mental disorders?
reframed_question: Can a transdiagnostic, mechanism-guided, adaptive care system improve treatment matching and durability for heterogeneous psychiatric presentations?

evidence_capsules.claim: Symptom heterogeneity, comorbidity, and context motivate transdiagnostic biomarker approaches.
Inflammation can affect symptom-relevant circuits and is associated with differential response in a subset.
forbidden_use: treat inflammation as a diagnosis for every patient

evidence_capsules.claim: Imaging genomics can connect genetic variation and neurobiological traits for translational precision medicine.
A transdiagnostic internalizing cohort can be randomized to SSRI or CBT and can show modality-specific neural correlates.
forbidden_use: claim a universal SSRI or CBT predictor

evidence_capsules.claim: Closed-loop psychiatric treatment may improve patient specificity, but meaningful titration biomarkers remain difficult.
RDoC-style dimensional constructs link neurobiology and observable behavior across diagnoses.

subhypotheses.claim: A multimodal transdiagnostic model improves out-of-sample trajectory prediction over diagnosis-only and symptom-only baselines.
Mechanism strata moderate treatment response and calibration rather than producing one universal biomarker.
Repeated response signals improve treatment-switch timing and reduce avoidable nonresponse under clinician supervision.
Utility gains persist under site-held-out, demographic subgroup, and missing-modality validation.
